observations: Photo 0 and photo 1: one white game console wrapped in clear plastic film, held by a hand in front of a shop window.
Photo 0 and photo 1: the Xbox sphere logo is on the front face and the top and side carry the fine dotted vent grille of the white Xbox One S body.
Photo 0 and photo 1: the front face looks plain with no disc slot or eject button visible, which fits the All-Digital Edition, but the plastic film and glare stop this being certain.
No controllers, power cable, HDMI cable or receipt appear in either photo.
The back panel, ports, serial sticker and any warranty seal are not shown; the console is not shown switched on.
Both photos carry a shop watermark and the background is a gadget shop display, so this is likely a dealer listing.

read_from: photo 0 Xbox logo on front face
photo 1 white dotted One S body with plain front

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show the white Xbox One S body and a front with no visible disc slot, but the plastic film hides detail and the label on the back is not shown.
The body looks clean under plastic film in photos 0 and 1, but the film can hide scratches and the back is not shown.
No photo of the back screws or warranty seal; even an intact seal cannot fully prove no repair.
Cannot be seen in photos; only a long running session would show it.
The back panel and ports are not shown and the console is not shown powered on.
No controller appears in either photo.

risks.risk: Console does not boot, or has a faulty power supply, HDMI port or hard drive.
risks.proof: A clip of the console being switched on, booting to the home screen on a TV, then opening Settings > System > Console info.

risks.risk: Controllers are missing or are copies, not original Microsoft pads.
risks.proof: A photo of the controllers beside the console, then a clip of one pairing and moving the cursor on screen.

risks.risk: Account ban or console ban, or console still tied to another owner's account.
risks.proof: A clip signing in and opening the Microsoft Store from the console.

risks.risk: Back panel damage, missing power cable or broken seal.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the back panel with the serial sticker and ports, plus the power and HDMI cables.
risks.if_unproven: as console only with no cables

proof_requests: Clip of the console powering on to the home screen and showing Console info.
Photo of the back panel, serial sticker and ports with film removed.
Photo of the controllers and cables beside the console, and a controller in use on screen.
Photo of the receipt beside the console serial sticker.
response.reason: The Xbox logo and white Xbox One S body are visible in photos 0 and 1, and the All-Digital Edition is the lowest-value variant, so it can be priced as that console alone, not working and without controllers. A boot clip and photos of the pads and cables would raise it.
